close_reason: Added # Runtime requirement section to Dispatcher::dispatch doc, paralleling the existing Cancellation block. Decoupling the spawn mechanism via Spawner trait is a major-bump API change tracked separately.
description:
crate-jmap-server/src/lib.rs:228-318 — Dispatcher::dispatch invokes
each handler under `tokio::task::spawn` (lib.rs:263) for panic
isolation. This implicitly binds the dispatcher to the tokio runtime
ecosystem.

The trait bounds visible to a consumer reading the dispatch signature:

    pub async fn dispatch(
        &self,
        request: JmapRequest,
        caller: CallerCtx,
        session_state: State,
    ) -> JmapResponse

…and the impl bounds on the inherent impl:

    impl<CallerCtx: Clone + Send + 'static> Dispatcher<CallerCtx> { … }

Neither surface mentions tokio. A consumer reading the signature
reasonably assumes the dispatcher works under any async runtime that
satisfies the `Send + 'static` bound — async-std, smol, embassy
(loosely), monoio. In fact, `tokio::task::spawn` panics if no tokio
runtime is current.

What callers cannot depend on:

1. That this is a runtime-agnostic async API. It is tokio-specific
   by design, but the design is not surfaced in the type system.

2. That the runtime requirement won't change. Future revisions
   could swap `tokio::task::spawn` for `tokio::task::spawn_local`
   (single-threaded runtime), `JoinSet`-based concurrency
   (different cancellation story), or `catch_unwind` (no tokio
   dep). Each shift changes what consumers must provide.

What goes wrong when this stays as-is:

- A consumer running their async stack on smol/async-std calls
  dispatch() and panics at the first method call with a tokio
  runtime-not-found error. The error is not obviously caused by
  the dispatcher.

- A consumer running tokio's `current_thread` runtime hits the
  task::spawn requirement that the spawned future is `Send` — they
  cannot use a `!Send` CallerCtx even though their runtime allows
  it.

- The Cargo.toml dep `tokio = { workspace = true }` is the only
  signal that tokio is required at runtime; consumers checking
  `cargo tree` will see it, but consumers reading the dispatch
  doc comment will not.

Resolution paths (one is sufficient):

- Add an explicit "Requires a tokio runtime" note to
  Dispatcher::dispatch's doc comment as a top-level "# Runtime"
  section, paralleling the existing "# Cancellation" section.
  (Low cost; documents what currently isn't documented.)

- Add a compile-time assert in tests/ that imports tokio's
  runtime check, so the trait bound is reflected at least in
  integration tests.

- Abstract the spawn mechanism behind a trait
  `Dispatcher::with_spawner(impl Spawner)` so consumers can plug
  their own runtime. (High cost; large API change.)

The narrow doc-only fix is the right scope for the current
review. The structural fix is a major-bump item.

The runtime-coupling concern is structural and locks the kit
into one async ecosystem. Even if tokio remains canonical for
JMAP, the kit should advertise the requirement, not bury it.
title: Dispatcher::dispatch implicitly requires a Tokio runtime via task::spawn — no compile-time signal
